Is studying abroad in UK worth it for Indian students?

As Indian students, we’re often met with two questions that everyone seems to be dying to know the answer to – 1) why should I study abroad? 2) which country should I choose to study in? While these are both valid and important questions, it’s worth remembering that no matter where you choose to study abroad, there will always be advantages and disadvantages. So before you embark on your international student journey, keep these things in mind as you decide whether or not study abroad in UK is worth it for Indian students. Study Abroad India offers quality degree programs and a wide range of options to choose from. There are also plenty of opportunities to work after graduation. But is studying abroad in UK really worth it, or should you consider staying back in India instead? Here’s what you need to know

The guide

Study Abroad in U.K.

The Study abroad in UK campaign was a joint initiative by British Council, Department of Education and Science and Higher Education Funding Council for England. The aim of these three bodies was to urge potential overseas students to see what U.K has to offer when it comes to top class higher education. Britain offers world class universities that provide challenging courses and excellent learning environments. It is no wonder why so many people look at Britain as their first choice when it comes to study abroad destinations. Students who have studied in U.K have time and again praised its educational system; they have also had nothing but good things to say about campus life too! Studying in Britain is certainly one of those ‘must do’ kind of things if you’re looking to pursue an international degree program today!

    Cost of Studying Abroad in UK

    Cost is a major consideration when studying abroad. Expenses such as tuition fees, living costs, visa application fees and travel expenses must be planned and budgeted before you leave. The cost of studying varies according to where you want to study, so it’s essential to do your research first. Compare tuition fees at institutions of your choice and find out what kind of financial aid is available. The average annual fee at top universities is around £9000-£12000 (£2000-3000 per year). However, some may ask for higher tuition fees. Check whether they offer any

    scholarships

    that are open to international students or have an exchange program with any foreign institution. These programs can save up to 50% on your overall costs!

    Living Expenses

    Most of us don’t realize just how much a life overseas can cost. While tuition may be comparable, or even lower than studying at home, and overall quality may be better, there are many other costs you’ll want to plan for – especially if you want to stay living overseas after graduation. There will be extra costs added to your living expenses that come with studying abroad. Just because they weren’t included in your education doesn’t mean they won’t be part of it. Before you take any more loans out, sit down and crunch some numbers with

      —it could end up saving you serious cash down the road.

        How to apply for a study visa?

        Applying for a study visa doesn’t have to be difficult. Just follow these steps: 1. Gather your documents 2. Choose a school 3. Apply! We know it sounds simple, but we also know that students are sometimes overwhelmed by what needs to be done and where to start. To help make studying abroad easier for you, we created an online application tool with step-by-step instructions on how to apply for a study visa. opt for our free counselling session and we will direct you through everything you need to get started on your new adventure of studying abroad in UK. Our team is available on calls or email if you have any questions along the way.

          What is the duration of a study visa?

          If you’re planning to study abroad in UK, you’ll need a student visa. The length of time your student visa lasts depends on whether you’re studying a full-time course or part-time. Full-time courses will require a Tier 4 (General) Student Visa while part-time courses may require an extended Tier 4 (Child) Student Visa. In order to apply for these visas, you must be enrolled at a university that has been authorized by Her Majesty’s Home Office. These schools are known as Designated Schools. Currently there are over 600 Designated Schools throughout England, Scotland and Wales. It’s important to note that when studying at a non-designated school, you might still qualify for a visa but it’s important to check with your school first before applying. This is because if they aren’t listed as Designated then they aren’t allowed to offer any type of degree/qualification that can be used towards immigration purposes.

            What are the documents required to apply for UK Student Visa from India?

            To apply for UK student visa, you will need a letter of acceptance from your school or college confirming that you have been accepted and that there is space available to study. You will also need an ID card, like a passport or driver’s license, with at least six months left before expiry. If you are under 18, parents must provide parental consent. All documents should be translated into English. Without these documents, applications may be delayed by many weeks or months.

              Can you work with UK Student Visa?

              Yes, you can work with a student visa provided that your Tier 4 visa is not yet expired. The Tier 4 visa allows you to study full-time at a registered and certified educational institution and work part-time during vacation periods. You can check if your employer is licensed by going through their website. You will also need to inform your Tier 4 sponsor about any job offers you receive so they can report back to UKVI (UK Visas & Immigration). Your sponsor must send them official written confirmation of your employment within 14 days of being informed of it. If they fail to do so, they could lose their sponsor license which means future international students sponsored by them will have no recourse but to find another education institution as their main Tier 4 Sponsor.

                International Opportunities

                There are lots of ways you can take advantage of studying at university level. You can immerse yourself in a new culture, broaden your horizons, and build a social network; on top of gaining valuable knowledge and experience. However, one question you should ask yourself is: is studying abroad in UK worth it? And how does that compare to staying at home and going to college back home?

                Conclusion

                While there are a ton of benefits to study abroad in UK. Deciding whether or not to move out of your home country can be difficult. Ultimately, you want to ask yourself if studying abroad is worth it for your career and personal goals. In many cases, moving overseas may prove to be an exceptional experience and aid you in achieving a successful future—but only if you plan ahead carefully. Think about your end goal first: do you intend on working back at home or staying overseas long-term?
